Subject: UK addendum exception and scoped TIA mapping for MediAssist

Hi Emma / Tom —

Thanks for taking time yesterday. Per our conversation: MediAssist needs a scoped Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) that reflects two constraints you mentioned — a small set of telemetry logs routed for analytics and the primary clinical data that must remain within EU/UK controls. To keep the legal path straightforward we attached a short TIA summary (MediAssist_TIA_Scoped_Summary.pdf) and our proposed redlines to the UK addendum (proposed-uk-addendum-redlines.docx).

Two asks to help us close quickly (target: sign by mid-December):
- Can you confirm whether any of your subprocessors currently process UK-personal data outside the UK/EU? Please provide a current subprocessor list and the location of processing for each.
- If you need a narrow routing exception for pseudonymized analytics logs, please outline the exact fields and retention so we can evaluate safeguards.

I copied Vivek (privacy lead) and Karthik (legal ops) — they will propose a limited mitigation if full IDTA/UK addendum coverage is not available.

Attachments: MediAssist_TIA_Scoped_Summary.pdf, proposed-uk-addendum-redlines.docx

Emma — quick follow up from privacy: we appreciate the detail. Two clarifications from Redwood's side:

1) We cannot grant a broad "UK routing exception". If telemetry or logs containing any personal identifiers will leave the UK/EU, we need appropriate safeguards — either SCCs + UK IDTA addendum (signed) or an explicit limited TIA that documents technical controls (pseudonymization, strict retention, encryption-in-transit and at-rest with customer-controlled keys).

2) For a narrow analytics exception we would accept: a) only pseudonymized session identifiers (no patient IDs), b) maximum retention 30 days, c) processing restricted to a specific Redwood project and team, and d) audit logs enabled with quarterly review. If that is acceptable, we can scope those items into the TIA summary and proceed to an abbreviated legal review.

Also, please share the subprocessor locations (DataCorp entry flagged). We will confirm whether a fallback to EU region routing is possible for clinical datasets. Linking the HubSpot record here for internal tracking: https://hubspot.company/contacts/MA-778.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Emma — forwarding our proposed redlines with inline comments (see attached proposed-uk-addendum-redlines.docx). A couple of practical points:

- If your legal team prefers, we can do a short 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the suggested language and the narrow TIA conditions Vivek outlined. That tends to speed approvals.
- We will prepare a DocuSign packet once redlines converge; tentative link: https://app.docusign.com/MA-778/doc/92jh.

On the routing question you raised: Redwood's hosted offering supports per-customer region pinning. For clinical datasets we recommend pinning to the UK/EU region and allowing analytics pseudonymized logs to be processed in a separate, auditable project (as Vivek outlined). If MediAssist can confirm the exact fields and retention, we will bake that into the TIA and proceed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — let us know best time for a call.

Regards,
